companies.latest_signal: Alibaba's June-quarter 2026 filing states Taobao Instant Commerce 'continued to improve its unit economics quarter-over-quarter, driven by higher average order value and enhanced fulfillment logistics efficiency, while maintaining market share.' Separate analyst estimates (CICC/中金, via 21jingji.com, not company-disclosed) put standalone Taobao Flash Sale EBITA at roughly -RMB36.7bn in Q3 2025 narrowing to -RMB21.1bn in Q4 2025, consistent with the segment-level trend.

companies.latest_signal: Loss narrowed both sequentially (-10.35bn to -9.85bn) and sharply YoY (from -14.78bn); CFO 许冉 (Sandy Xu) attributed the improvement to per-order subsidy discipline and delivery-network efficiency, with 网易/163.com reporting '京东外卖亏损减少超过50%' (JD Takeaway losses down over 50% YoY), Aug 13 2026.

war_summary: Subsidy war peaked in Q2-Q3 2025 (combined platform subsidy spend exceeding RMB100bn in one half-year; ~RMB150bn cumulative one-year burn per 虎嗅/huxiu.com) but has clearly de-escalated since: Beijing's SAMR turned its 'anti-involution' (反内卷) campaign explicitly on the platforms from March 2026 ('外卖大战该结束了'), followed by a June 17 2026 draft rulebook capping predatory subsidies, and by June 29-30 2026 Meituan, Taobao Flash Purchase and JD Takeaway reached a joint consensus to moderate subsidies (Guancha.cn/Sina Finance). Alibaba was the original aggressor and spent most aggressively, but its YoY EBITA erosion narrowed fastest (-76% to roughly flat within four quarters), suggesting it blinked first even as it maintains a ~RMB1tn instant-commerce GMV ambition; order share has stabilized near 55:45 Meituan:Taobao Flash Purchase with JD under 10%.
